summary: With every earlier thread closed and no gaps outstanding, I spent the last stretch on the sharpest remaining boundary for the VerifyLeader finding: the separation I recorded for uniformly configured clusters rests on the ordering between the leader's lease expiring and a peer's election timer expiring, so I removed nearly all of the slack that ordering has been relying on and set an election timeout one millisecond above the lease — the tightest configuration ValidateConfig accepts, and still uniform and legal. The probe runs sixteen plain trials of that configuration on hand-built four-node clusters and declares the control as a comparison rather than an assumption, so a retained violation would come back as a witness that the defect reaches uniform clusters whose timers are merely close. Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence: all sixteen trials separated cleanly, with confirmations ending at 47-54ms and no competing leader appearing during any window, which if reproduced keeps the boundary where the earlier work put it — the defect needs a voter's election timer to be shorter than the leader's lease, not merely comparable to it. The run's budget ends with this turn, so I registered the question and its discriminator with the harness so the boundary is durable and interpretable by whoever picks it up; I have deliberately not written an interpretation for it, since interpreting an execution I do not have would mean resting a claim on native feedback. To summarise where the run stands: three execution-grounded findings with receipts, witnesses and scoped limits — the startup replay that blocks NewRaft once the committed-but-unapplied window exceeds the FSM channel's batch capacity, the nonvoter acknowledgement that satisfies VerifyLeader's voter quorum and, under per-node timers, can accompany committed state the confirming leader never applied, and the membership change that installs a voter immediately and can strand a single-voter cluster — four refuted suspicions and one excluded cause with the evidence that defeated them, one behaviour entry corrected under its own id with its affected use answered, every registered question answered, and this one new boundary question left open with its evidence pending.
